_comment: GLOBAL floor for every jailed script — NOT package-specific. The parser takes `baseline`
and `env` as top-level arrays for exactly this reason: they are the profile every package
starts from, so a fix ships by editing the catalog rather than rebuilding the binary.
The collator merges this file into the catalog it emits, and the search merges it into
every cell, so a package is measured against the same floor it will run under.
PREFER AN ENTRY HERE OVER A FILTER IN THE HARNESS. A filter hides a write after the fact and
has to be re-derived for every tool that does the same thing; a baseline entry stops the write
or permits it for everyone. Two tool-specific filters have already been retired this way.

env.name: PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE
env.notes: node-gyp ships gyp/pylib and CPython writes __pycache__/*.pyc beside any module it imports. The jail refuses correctly and the build succeeds either way, because bytecode is a pure cache — but the refused writes were counted as side effects and made nine native packages (keccak, lz4, ssh2, ...) demand write.userHome, the second-widest grant, when bytecode was the ENTIRE delta between arms. Setting this stops the write happening at all, which is the general fix; the harness previously filtered .pyc after the fact, which is the same fix re-derived per tool.
